question: Is there an instance-level, verifiable record of commercial drone use in Ukraine and of AI in military operations — thousands of individual occurrences, each with a citation — or only aggregate claims from parties to the conflict?
refusal: This file publishes no tally, no loss figure, no casualty number and no dollar amount. It records only whether a source answered, in what shape, and roughly how many rows it appears to carry. A probe log that quoted a loss count beside a URL would be a casualty claim with a filename where a citation should be.
note: Loss records like Oryx are undercounts by construction: a vehicle nobody photographed is not in the list. That is a feature for citability and a trap for comparison — the two sides are photographed at different rates by different numbers of people with different phones and different reasons to post. Any page built on this must say so in the same breath as the number.

findings.what: Oryx, Russian equipment losses, one entry per photographed item
findings.settles: Whether a per-item, photo-linked loss record can be read by a script at all

findings.what: Oryx, Ukrainian equipment losses, the mirror list
findings.settles: Whether both sides can be read the same way, so neither is the only side shown

findings.what: USAspending, the product and service code tree
findings.settles: Whether contracts can be filtered by what was bought rather than by a keyword search

findings.what: USAspending, an award-by-id record, to see a single row's shape
findings.settles: What one award record carries, so a connector knows which fields exist

findings.what: AI Incident Database, the public snapshot index
findings.settles: Whether the incident corpus is downloadable in bulk rather than scraped
Whether incidents can be queried directly

findings.what: AIAAIC repository, the public spreadsheet as CSV
findings.settles: Whether a thousand-row incident register with a military sector exists as machine-readable text

findings.what: UCDP georeferenced events, Ukraine, one year
findings.settles: Whether a per-event, geolocated, source-cited conflict dataset is keyless

findings.what: ACLED, which classifies drone strikes as their own event subtype
findings.settles: Whether ACLED answers without a key — it is the only source that types a drone strike as such

findings.what: List of equipment of the Ukrainian Ground Forces
findings.settles: Whether an equipment list gives a per-type table a script can read

findings.what: Unmanned aerial vehicles in the Russo-Ukrainian War
findings.settles: Whether there is a single article indexing the UAV types in this war
